title: Variable Types in Action
subtitle: Handle floating-point, long, and String declarations under more pressure.
objective: Catch each correct token set and arrange every Java variable declaration before mistakes run out.

rounds.prompt: Build a valid float variable declaration for temperature.
hints: A float literal often ends with the letter f.
Keep the type keyword at the beginning.
The variable name should explain the value being stored.

rounds.prompt: Build a valid long variable declaration for population.
hints: Long values can use an L suffix.
Do not wrap numeric literals in quotation marks.
A declaration needs type, name, equals, value, semicolon.

rounds.prompt: Build a valid String variable declaration for course.
hints: Strings store text inside double quotation marks.
The word Variables is the value, not the variable name.
Put the semicolon at the very end.
